title: NZ Ski Holiday Cost Calculator
description: Real 2026 lift pass, gear hire, and accommodation prices for Queenstown, Wanaka, and Mt Ruapehu — work out what a family ski trip actually costs.
html_content:
Your NZ Ski Trip Cost

Estimated Total Cost

Where these numbers come from: Lift pass prices are current official adult/child full-day rates — Coronet Peak & The Remarkables (NZSki Superpass, adult $180, child 6–15 $60, under 6 free), Cardrona & Treble Cone (adult $184 online day rate; child rate derived from the resort's published 2-day child pass), and Whakapapa on Mt Ruapehu (adult $95, child/youth blended from the resort's published $45 ages 5–9 / $65 ages 10–17 tiers) — checked August 2026. Gear hire rates are from Queenstown/Wanaka rental pricing (standard package $40 adult / $25 child per day). Ski school, on-mountain food, accommodation and travel distance are reasonable estimates grounded in our full Skiing in NZ with Kids guide and NZ driving-times data — actual prices vary by date, advance booking, and season, and change through the year, so confirm at the field before you book.

faq.question: How much does a family ski trip cost in NZ?
faq.answer: For a family of 4 (2 adults, 2 children) skiing 3 days at Coronet Peak or The Remarkables with standard gear hire, ski school for the kids, and budget accommodation, expect roughly $2,500–$3,500 for the trip excluding flights. Lift passes alone run $450–$550/day for a family of 4. Use the calculator above for a personalised estimate based on your field, group size and days.

faq.question: Which NZ ski field is cheapest for families?
faq.answer: Whakapapa on Mt Ruapehu (North Island) has the lowest lift pass prices — adult day passes from $95 versus $180 at Coronet Peak/The Remarkables and $184+ at Cardrona. Accommodation around Ruapehu (National Park, Ohakune) is also generally cheaper than Queenstown or Wanaka in peak season.

faq.question: Is it cheaper to buy NZ ski lift passes online in advance?
faq.answer: Yes. Most NZ fields — including Coronet Peak, The Remarkables and Cardrona — offer a discount of roughly 10-15% for lift passes bought online ahead of your visit compared with walk-up ticket window prices.

faq.question: How much is ski gear hire in Queenstown or Wanaka?
faq.answer: A standard adult ski or snowboard package (skis or board, boots, poles) typically costs around $40/day, with premium/advanced packages around $65/day. Children's packages are typically around $25/day. Hiring on-mountain at the field is usually more convenient than hiring in town.
